evidence: The round-0 hunk shows the catch path re-checking `token !== this.sessionSelectToken` while the success path fires select-window/select-pane with no check, so a superseded jump's absolute-target selects still run; b2ff341 adds the guard after the await plus a supersession test.
guidance_note: When a token guards one settlement arm of an async operation, put the check once after the await so every arm (success and failure) passes through it.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 at a different line: same unguarded success path after `await switch-client`; the agent correctly folded it into the single b2ff341 fix.

The field comment says the token is bumped on new requests and selectPane only, and `stop()` reset `suggest` without bumping it, so a late llm reply passes the token check; b2ff341 routes both stop and selectPane through `clearSuggestion()`, which fixes the whole class.
guidance_note: When adding an invalidation token, enumerate every site that resets the guarded state and route them all through one helper before the first push.

evidence: Flag false positive: b2ff341 touched only store.ts and copilot-store files, and the allSettled loop with no failed count is round-0 code. Premise holds because a rejected pane was counted as neither sent nor blocked. The agent accepted despite the pushback hint, and 484085c also counts fulfilled `{success:false}` as failed.
guidance_note: When a summary derives from Promise.allSettled, give every outcome arm (fulfilled-ok, fulfilled-error, rejected) its own field in the summary type, so no attempted item can vanish.

evidence: Flag false positive: broadcast-store.test.ts was created in the original PR with a verbatim copy of Deferred/deferred/tick, and b2ff341 did not touch it. The duplication is real, and 484085c extracted test-utils.ts.
guidance_note: Before copying a helper into a new test file, grep for existing copies and extract a shared module instead.

evidence: The round-0 jumpToPane awaits switch-client inside try/catch and never reads `.success`, while the reviewer cites ws-client.ts:329 for %error resolving with success:false. The gap is in the original rewrite, not in b2ff341's one-line token guard, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When gating follow-on commands on a command's success, check the response's success field as well as the promise, because this bridge reports tmux %error as a resolved value.

evidence: The original tests covered only a rejected switch-client and missed the success:false path F6 identifies. This companion to F6 is a gap in the original PR, not in b2ff341 (flag false positive), and 484085c adds the test.
guidance_note: Write one test per failure representation the transport can produce (reject and resolved-error) when testing a short-circuit.

evidence: 484085c created test-utils.ts claiming the helpers 'live here once' but migrated only three test files. The 0b134bc diff shows console-store.test.ts and escape-playground-store.test.ts still held identical local deferred/tick.
guidance_note: When extracting a duplicated helper, grep the whole package for every copy, not just the files the reviewer named, before claiming one source of truth.

evidence: Flag false positive: 0b134bc only migrated test imports, and the round-1 summary already called the copilot-store await pre-existing. The 'never throws' contract is real but enforced at HttpLlmClient (per the agent, llm-client.ts:34-51, not shown in the packet), so the stuck-loading risk is hypothetical and a second catch would duplicate the enforcer.

narrative: Round 0 found real gaps in the token guards (an unguarded success path, and stop() not invalidating). Round 1 found the original jumpToPane rewrite ignoring `{success:false}` and the broadcast summary dropping failed panes, all original-PR gaps. Round 2 existed only because the test-utils extraction covered three of five duplicating files. Round 3 was a pre-existing contract concern that the agent correctly declined.
guidance_observations: The agent repeatedly treated 'promise resolved' as 'command succeeded' on a bridge that resolves %error. Knowing that transport contract before writing the first await would have removed F6 and F7 and shaped F4.

The agent's fixes generalized well (clearSuggestion, failedPanes counting %error). The sweep for the duplicated helper was the one fix scoped to the reviewer's named files instead of a repo-wide grep.

evidence: The PR is titled 'SCRATCH: verify CI red on broken bench gate (do not merge)' and was closed unmerged. `expect(1).toBe(2)` is the deliberate red-check, so 'must be removed before merge' misreads the PR's purpose. Leaving it unanswered was fine, and should_have is set to pushed_back only because the enum has no no_response value.

narrative: This was a deliberate scratch PR to prove the bench gate turns CI red once continue-on-error was removed. The reviewer correctly saw that the assertion always fails but treated the intended failure as a bug. The PR was closed without merge.
guidance_observations: A scratch verification PR draws automated review cost. Opening it as a draft, or labeling it so the reviewer skips it, would avoid a meaningless finding.

evidence: The hunk shows the prior line was `void this.runReseed()`, so this PR did not change rejection semantics; it only added the microtask defer. The claim that capture-pane failures are caught in seed() (pane-stream.ts:552-566) is not visible in the packet. The agent concedes a real residual (a throwing listener aborts the sweep) and defers it to 'its own ticket' without filing one.
guidance_note: When conceding a real but out-of-scope residual during a pushback, file the ticket and link it in the reply instead of saying it 'deserves its own ticket'.

narrative: This was a single-round review of a one-line microtask defer. The one advisory blamed the PR for unhandled-rejection behavior that the diff shows was unchanged from before. The agent's pushback correctly scoped it out and acknowledged the residual sweep-abort property.
guidance_observations: The acknowledged residual (one throwing target aborts the reseed sweep) was left untracked, because the reply described a ticket but did not file one.

evidence: The README sentence 'the 4 exemptions are the linked-window %window-close variant and the flow-control trio ..., which require backpressure' attaches the backpressure clause ambiguously. 7ef7649 gives each exemption its own reason.
In the round-0 hunk, `waitForEvent` gained a timeout and reject while the new `waitReady` right below it has neither. 7ef7649 adds the same timeout pattern.
guidance_note: When adding a timeout to one wait helper, give every sibling wait helper in the file the same treatment in the same edit.

evidence: Duplicate of F2 (waitReady has no timeout). It was handled by the same 7ef7649 change.

`COVERAGE[name].kind` would throw a TypeError on a missing key, but the sibling catalogue-integrity test already asserts keys equal §23, so the gap is only a worse error message. Iterating `Object.entries(COVERAGE)` removes the undefined path without duplicating the integrity check.

The reviewer's 'falsely pass' claim is wrong: a dropped spec row would make spec23 differ from WIRE_MESSAGE_TYPES, so integrity reddens, as the agent itself noted. Failing at the parse is still a cheaper diagnostic, and 7ef7649 broadens the class and throws on unparseable rows.

Flag false positive: 2c4fb80 only moved config-error to exempt and trimmed imports, while the c2 probes with happy-path-only `c2.close()` are original-PR code. The leak is real, and 7ef7649's withSecondClient closes c2 in a finally.
guidance_note: When a test spawns a secondary process or client, write its lifecycle as try/finally (or a with-helper) from the start, so an early throw cannot skip cleanup.

evidence: Duplicate of F6 on the same c2 lifecycle, and the same false-positive flag (2c4fb80 did not touch the probes). It was fixed by withSecondClient in 7ef7649.
This re-raises F2 (waitReady has no timeout) because round 1 reviewed 2c4fb80 before the 7ef7649 fix was pushed. 2c4fb80 never touched waitReady, so the flag is a false positive.

This duplicates F6 (c2 is not closed when the probe throws), with the same false-positive flag. The probe's failure itself is loud, and the defect is a leaked process, which is resource lifecycle rather than a swallowed failure, so the no-silent-failure citation echoes the reviewer's tag instead of fitting the defect.

The error probe's `void client.execute("this-is-not-a-command").catch(() => {})` would swallow a transport error and leave `await p` to hang until timeout. 7ef7649 rethrows anything that is not a TmuxCommandError. This is original-PR code, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Never write a bare `.catch(() => {})` on an expected rejection; assert the expected error type and rethrow everything else.

evidence: The F10 fix in 7ef7649 repaired the discarded execute promise in the error probe only. The %output probe's `void client.execute("send-keys ...")` in the same COVERAGE table, the same class of discarded provocation promise, was left for round 2.
guidance_note: When fixing a discarded or swallowed promise in one probe, grep every probe in the table for `void client.execute` and fix them all in the same commit.

evidence: Flag false positive: ef2bc3e only changed the %output probe, and the runner's `client?.close()` in finally is original. Close is idempotent today, so the reviewer's concern is hypothetical, and the reviewer itself offered 'document the invariant'. The agent did that in 855615d instead of coupling the generic runner to the exit probe.

The F2 fix (7ef7649) gave `waitReady` a 12s timeout but left `createSession`'s identical connection-state→ready wait untimed. The live runner calls createSession, so a hung attach still skipped the finally cleanup. Fixed in e4a4c20 by delegating to waitReady.
guidance_note: When hardening a wait helper, search for every other place that waits on the same event (here, createSession's ready wait) and collapse them onto the hardened helper.

narrative: Rounds 0 and 1 surfaced genuine original-PR gaps in the test harness: missing timeouts, leaked second clients, and a bare catch. Round 1 also re-raised findings whose fixes were not yet pushed. Round 2 existed because the swallowed-promise fix covered the error probe but not the %output probe. Round 4 existed because the waitReady timeout fix missed createSession's duplicate readiness wait. Round 3 was a hypothetical fragility that the agent answered by documenting the invariant.
guidance_observations: Both avoidable rounds came from fixing exactly the instance named rather than sweeping the file for the same pattern (`void client.execute`, connection-state ready waits).
The round-1 findings were raised against 2c4fb80 before 7ef7649 was pushed, so several duplicates reflect push timing rather than new defects.

evidence: The new e2e job had no `timeout-minutes`, so a hang would run to GitHub's 360-minute default. 1c9addb adds a 15-minute cap and cites the observed ~1.5-minute runtime.
guidance_note: When adding a CI job that launches GUI or external processes, set timeout-minutes in the same commit, sized from the measured runtime.

evidence: Flag false positive: 1c9addb only touched ci.yml, and `b.elements.every(...)` in importClauseIsTypeOnly is original-PR code. An empty array makes `every` vacuously true, so `import {} from "m"` was classed as type-only. 6406165 adds a `length > 0` guard and a node:dns regression case.
guidance_note: When writing a classifier over AST node lists, put the empty-list case in the accept/reject table explicitly, because `every([])` is true.

evidence: This is the export-side twin of F2, raised in the same round: `node.exportClause.elements.every(...)` vacuously classes `export {} from "m"` as type-only. It is original-PR code, and 1c9addb (ci.yml only) did not touch it.

The agent forced a failure and observed traces at repo-root `./test-results/...`, which matches the upload `path: test-results/` when the job runs from the repo root. Playwright's default outputDir is relative to the package root, not the config file. 6406165 touched only the unit test, so the flag is a false positive.

narrative: Round 0's only finding was a missing CI timeout. Round 1 found a real vacuous-truth bug, on both the import and export side, in the original AST edge collector; it was not caused by the timeout fix. Round 2's trace-path claim was wrong, and the agent refuted it by reproducing the failure.
guidance_observations: The empirical check on F4 (forcing a failure to see where traces land) is the right way to settle a reviewer's claim about tool behavior.

evidence: The catch reported unconditionally while success was epoch-gated, so a superseded bootstrap could raise a false alarm. The proposed `isBootstrapCurrent` guard would also have swallowed a genuine failure bumped only by `invalidateWindow`. The agent's `isLatestBootstrap` covers that case, as the redesign-laws test diverging on window-close shows.
guidance_note: When adding a failure report to an epoch-guarded async path, list every staleness source (newer start, window invalidation, transport close, reconnect) and decide each one before the first push.

evidence: The renderer's `else` branch cast every non-connection-state message `as TmuxMessage` into handleNotification, including synthetic events; 3fe8f13 narrows it with `isTmuxMessage`. The finding also said main's `broadcast` forwards topology-error to renderers, and the fix left that half unaddressed.
guidance_note: When a finding names two facts, here the cast and main's broadcast forwarding the new event, address or explicitly scope out each one in the plan.

evidence: A bare `close 1006` message carries no bootstrap context, which is a diagnosability issue rather than a bug. 3fe8f13 wraps it at the router seam as 'topology bootstrap failed: ...' and keeps `.cause`, which serves every transport.

Duplicate of F1. Here the reviewer's own scenario involves window-close bumping bootstrapGen, which is exactly the case where its proposed `isBootstrapCurrent` guard would suppress a real failure. The agent's isLatestBootstrap guard handles it.

Flag false positive: the required `reportTopologyError` constructor param dates from the original commit, while 3fe8f13 only changed guards and error wrapping. TopologyRouter is public, so the break is real. The agent rejected the no-op default, which would restore silent drops, and documented the break in CHANGELOG in 7c6ae90.
guidance_note: When changing an exported constructor or function signature, record the break in CHANGELOG in the same commit.

evidence: The Symbol example is wrong (`String(Symbol('x'))` returns 'Symbol(x)'), but a null-prototype object or throwing toString does make `String(value)` throw. That coercion already existed in the pre-fix `toError`, so 3fe8f13's rename to bootstrapError carried it over rather than introducing it, and the flag is a false positive. 7c6ae90 makes it total.
guidance_note: Make any normalizer that runs inside a catch block total, guarding its own coercions, because a throw there turns a handled failure into an unhandled one.

evidence: The F1 fix (3fe8f13) suppressed stale failure reports for supersession by a newer bootstrap but not for transport close, so a bootstrap rejecting after onTransportClose still emitted topology-error after connection-state: closed. 7c6ae90 adds a `runCommand === null` guard.
guidance_note: When suppressing stale failure reports, enumerate every event that makes an in-flight attempt stale (supersession, close, reconnect), not just the one the reviewer named.

evidence: F2's text already said that main's `broadcast` (`client.on("*", broadcast)`) forwards the new topology-error to renderers. The F2 fix only replaced the cast, so the double-source emission was left for round 2, and eba5655 filters it at the forward seam.
guidance_note: When introducing a new event type into a bridge that forwards all events, decide at introduction time whether it should cross the bridge, and test that decision.

evidence: The renderer proxy's own topology-error wiring dates from the original PR and had no end-to-end failure test; eba5655 added only the negative forwarding test. The coverage gap predates the fix, so the flag is a false positive, and 6408547 adds the positive IPC test.
guidance_note: When adding a new failure-reporting seam in each transport adapter, add one end-to-end failure test per adapter in the original PR.

evidence: The reviewer itself calls the pending entries 'harmless in practice'. The agent explains that reconnect-window entries flush on welcome and are deleted on response, and that clearing on openSocket would reject legitimately queued commands. 6408547 touched only a test, so the flag is a false positive. The agent offered a follow-up ticket but did not file one.
guidance_note: When declining an out-of-scope hygiene concern, file the follow-up ticket instead of offering to.

evidence: The F7 fix's `this.runCommand === null` guard (7c6ae90) tests whether the slot is empty, so close-then-reopen leaves a new runner in place and the stale rejection reports. The agent concedes the websocket client never calls onTransportClose on reconnect, and f30f20f switches to identity `this.runCommand !== run`.
guidance_note: Guard staleness by comparing the identity of the captured resource rather than checking whether the slot is empty, and test the close-then-reopen (ABA) path.

evidence: The test 6408547 added for F9 used `for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) await Promise.resolve();`, which couples it to IPC microtask depth. The reviewer concedes the test is valid, and f30f20f rewrites it to await the event.
guidance_note: In async tests, await the observed event (a promise resolved in the handler) instead of flushing a fixed number of microtasks.

narrative: The stale-failure-suppression logic took three rounds to converge: supersession (F1), then transport close (F7), then close-then-reopen identity (F11). Each fix handled only the staleness source just named. Round 2 existed only because the F2 fix ignored the broadcast-forwarding half of the reviewer's own text. The agent's judgment was strong elsewhere: it rejected the naive isBootstrapCurrent guard, corrected the Symbol claim, and rejected the no-op default.
guidance_observations: Writing out every way an in-flight bootstrap becomes stale (newer start, window close, transport close, reconnect) at the first fix would have collapsed the F1→F7→F11 chain into one round.
Twice in this PR (F10, and implicitly F1's residual analysis) a follow-up ticket was offered or described but not filed.
